title: Small-batch release steward notes (safety + observability sketch)
content:
Context:
This is a working scratchpad for running very small, controlled feature activations (micro-batches) when shipping LLM-facing changes that touch routing, model selection, or response-safety heuristics. Aimed at product owners + release stewards + SRE oncall.

Goals:
- Surface early regressions with minimal user impact.
- Keep intervention simple: a single toggle or traffic-reroute should be enough to revert.
- Collect deterministic signals quickly (10-30m windows) for go/no-go decisions.
- Ensure cross-functional commitments are explicit (who watches what).

Definitions (quick):
- micro-batch: 0.1% to 1% of eligible requests (or a small explicit cohort), routed to the new codepath/model variant.
- steward: person responsible during the activation window (usually product owner or release engineer).
- safety signal: any Delta in hallucination rate, harmful content classifier score, or customer complaint spike.
- reliability signal: latency p50/p95, error rate, token generation truncations, 502/504 spikes.

Pre-activation checklist (must be green):
- [ ] Feature flag implemented with deterministic targeting (user id hash slice) and immediate kill-switch.
- [ ] Canary model variant deployed in staging that mirrors production config (quant, batch sizes). Link: github:pull/rlw/362
- [ ] Observability queries ready and verified on prod data schema:
    - SQL: SELECT slice, count(*) as requests, avg(latency_ms) as p50_latency FROM inference_requests WHERE env='prod' AND slice in ('control','candidate') GROUP BY slice;
    - Error metric: rate(status_code >= 500) by slice over 1m, 5m windows
    - Safety regressions: pct(harm_score>0.7) by slice over 30m
- [ ] Alert thresholds drafted and staged in alertmanager (see JIRA INFR-2124 for details).
- [ ] Stakeholders paged calendar: stewards, eng-oncall, safety-researcher, customer-success rep.
- [ ] Post-activation retrospective slot scheduled (30m within 2 business days).

Activation protocol (short):
1) Steward: announce start in #pg-rollouts and tag stakeholders.
2) Toggle traffic to 0.5% for first 15 minutes to candidate slice.
3) Watch these live panels:
   - per-slice p50/p95 latency (1m refresh)
   - per-slice error rate and HTTP 5xx counts
   - safety classifier score distribution and outlier examples (last 100 requests)
   - top-10 user-visible response diffs (sampling capture)
4) At 15m: quick decision meeting (2–3 min) - green = proceed; amber = hold and increase observability; red = rollback immediately.

Quick decision heuristics (example thresholds):
- Abort immediately (red) if any of:
  - 5xx rate in candidate slice > 2x control for two consecutive 1m windows OR absolute 5xx > 0.5%
  - p95 latency candidate > control p95 + 300ms for two consecutive intervals
  - safety metric: pct(harm_score>0.7) increases by > 0.5 percentage points AND absolute count > 5 in last 30m
  - any verified customer complaint (CS ticket opened referencing recent request ids) that clearly ties to candidate output
- Hold (amber) if:
  - metric drift is borderline (e.g., p95 +150–300ms) or small safety uptick without clear examples. In this case, keep at same exposure and expand sampling of raw responses for manual review.
- Proceed (green) if none of the above and sample-quality checks look OK after 30–60m.

Rollback steps (one-click ideal):
- Flip feature flag to route all traffic back to control slice.
- If flag doesn't propagate: execute emergency reroute in routing service CLI: reroute set model=baseline --slice-candidate=0.
- Page SRE and create a short incident note with the initial metrics snapshot.

Observability playbook (what to watch and how):
- Latency slices: p50/p95, token-generation-time, kv-cache hit rate.
- Errors: 5xx counts, decoder truncation errors, stream disconnects.
- Quality signals: safety classifier (distribution + examples), rerank/score deltas, eval prompts mismatch rate.
- Business signals: CS tickets and NPS blips (if instrumentation available in realtime).
- Canary noise filters: suppress false alarms from known transient infra events (link infra runbook).

Sampling and human review guidance:
- Capture 1:50 deterministic sample of candidate responses with request metadata (model, slice, prompt hash).
- Safety-researcher triage: review first 50 sample responses within 1 hour. Flag examples with IDs for CS.
- Annotator checklist: intent correctness, hallucination instances, policy-violating content, helpfulness score 1–5.

Cross-team responsibilities (during activation window):
- Steward (product): run the procedure, make go/no-go call, coordinate notes.
- Eng-oncall (SRE): watch infra signals, ready to rollback, owns reroute commands.
- Safety researcher: triage sample responses and advise.
- CS rep: monitor customer channels and triage complaints.
- Developer owning change: available for debug and fixes.

Post-mortem template (short):
- Summary (1–2 sentences)
- Activation parameters (slice %, model variant, flags)
- Time window and decision timeline
- Metrics snapshot (control vs candidate)
- Root cause hypothesis and action items (owner + ETA)
- Follow-up verification steps and regression tests added

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Q: Should we automate the 15m decision call via a small decision engine that evaluates metric deltas and recommends rollback? Pros: faster. Cons: risk of automated flip on noisy signals.
- Q: What's the minimal safe sample size for safety reviewer to be confident? Current rule of thumb = 50 but needs data-backed backing.
- TODO: add a simple synthetic prompt suite that targets known failure classes (hallucination prompts, policy edge-cases) and run it each activation for deterministic signal.
- TODO: add a tiny UI panel in Console that shows last 100 candidate vs control response pairs for quick human review.

Simulated scenario (example):
- Feature: new prefix-cache optimization + model quantized variant.
- Activation: 0.3% for 30 minutes targeting web-engaged users in us-west.
- Observed: p95 + 120ms at 10m, 5xx spike to 0.35% at 12m (baseline 0.08%). Safety classifier up +0.2pp but no concrete examples.
- Decision: steward holds exposure at 0.3%, requests developer to increase trace sampling and produce raw request/response for 1 hour. After 45m, with more examples, dev fixes a tokenization bug and we re-run a 0.5% activation.

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc short and pragmatic; link to longer runbooks for incident response and infra debugging.
- Iterate thresholds after 10 activations to calibrate noise vs real regressions.

References and links:
- Confluence: FEATURE-ROLLUP-938 (design spec)
- JIRA: INFR-2124 (alerts + routing hooks)
- GitHub PR: rlw/362 (model-serving opt)
- Slack: #pg-rollouts (active channel)

Signed-off-by: Ava Martinez (steward lead)
